title: Fetching Data from APIs knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a robust asynchronous API wrapper do?
options: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
Trust response.json() because its result is automatically verified by TypeScript.
Treat a declared response type as a server-side authorization check.
questions.answer_key: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.explanation: The type checker does not validate remote data; asynchronous operations can fail independently.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Fetching Data from APIs”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with fetch request and response types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with fetch request and response types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Fetch request and response types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Fetching Data from APIs”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check http status handling, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume typed api client functions is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check http status handling, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “HTTP status handling”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
